what: The ground loop detects its own code drift (staleness.diagnostics already does this) and RESPONDS by exiting cleanly, so the launcher respawns a fresh process. Two command flags in instance-space control the behavior: COMMAND_EXIT.flag (clean shutdown on any beat) and COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag (suppress the drift-triggered exit during development). The flags architecture: a permanent menu in <instance>/flags/ (ls to see what is available) and active signals as zero-byte COPIES in <instance>/ground_loop/ (the signal folder, same shape every device has). Touch to signal, rm to clear. The menu never empties because the signal is a copy, not a move.
why: The trouble ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges has count=207, firing every ~9s since 2026-08-18. The DETECTION is PROVED (staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk); the RESPONSE does not exist. The loop names its own staleness and blames nobody else, correctly — but it keeps running stale, accumulating trouble records, and holding modules that no longer match their files. This ticket is the response: the condition becomes transient because a stale loop restarts.
children: none, because the mechanism is three stat calls per beat (source mtime, two flag files) and one conditional exit — leaf-sized, no decomposition needed
state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(a_stale_loop_restarts_itself) -> PROVED
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a code change lands (any .py under cairn/ touched after process_started()) and the loop does NOT exit within one beat cycle after detecting it, unless COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag is active in the signal folder — the core property; (2) COMMAND_EXIT.flag in the signal folder and the loop does NOT exit within one beat cycle — the shutdown channel; (3) COMMAND_DO_NOT_RESTART.flag active and a code change detected, and the loop exits ANYWAY — the development hold; (4) the flags/ directory is missing a flag that the code checks — the menu is incomplete; (5) a flag check takes longer than 1ms (two stat calls on the signal folder per beat) — cost creep into the beat; (6) the trouble ground-loop-is-older-than-the-code-it-judges STILL fires after this build ships — the whole point, and the proof is running the loop, landing a code change, and verifying restart. WRONG INTENT if the flag mechanism becomes anything more than presence-based zero-byte files, or if the check examines anything beyond the signal folder per beat (scanning the flags/ menu on every beat wastes the distinction between definition and signal).
gates_bound: proof gate: cairn/devices/ground_loop/proofs/ (new proof testing flag response and restart-on-drift, runnable bare and under the tester). Charter gate: cairn/devices/ground_loop/intention+why.json delta for the self-restart mechanism and the flags architecture. Emission gate: the WATCHME probe, armed before the WATCHME crossing.
collision_check: staleness-is-about-this-process-not-about-disk (PROVED) — this ticket USES that predicates output and adds the ACT. the-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device (PROVED) — changed who gets blamed; this ticket changes what HAPPENS NEXT. DISTINCTION RECORDED: this ticket retires a standing trouble by making the condition transient.
distinctions_recorded: (1) The flags architecture is presence-based zero-byte files with a MENU/SIGNAL split: flags/ is definitions (permanent), ground_loop/ is active signals (transient copies). This is Akiens design, ruled 2026-08-19.
(2) The beat cadence IS the flag-response latency — currently ~8-9s. No sub-second response promised or needed.
(3) Restart means clean exit, not exec-in-place. The launcher (superclaude) already spawns; the respawn policy is the launchers concern, not the ground loops.
